name: Region Separation
description: There are $$$n$$$ cities in the Kingdom of Autumn, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. People can travel between any two cities using $$$n-1$$$ two-directional roads. This year, the government decides to separate the kingdom. There will be regions of different levels. The whole kingdom will be the region of level $$$1$$$. Each region of $$$i$$$-th level should be separated into several (at least two) regions of $$$i+1$$$-th level, unless $$$i$$$-th level is the last level. Each city should belong to exactly one region of each level and for any two cities in the same region, it should be possible to travel between them passing the cities in the same region only. According to research, for each city $$$i$$$, there is a value $$$a_i$$$, which describes the importance of this city. All regions of the same level should have an equal sum of city importances. Your task is to find how many plans there are to determine the separation of the regions that all the conditions are satisfied. Two plans are considered different if and only if their numbers of levels are different or there exist two cities in the same region of one level in one plan but in different regions of this level in the other plan. Since the answer may be very large, output it modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 10^6$$$) — the number of the cities. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers, the $$$i$$$-th of which is $$$a_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the value of each city. The third line contains $$$n-1$$$ integers, $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{n-1}$$$; $$$p_i$$$ ($$$p_i \leq i$$$) describes a road between cities $$$p_i$$$ and $$$i+1$$$.
output_specification: Print one integer — the number of different plans modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1034C — Region Separation [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
